newsitem.title: POLAND: Missed Polish '96 CPI goal not worrying -W.Bank.
newsitem.headline: Missed Polish '96 CPI goal not worrying -W.Bank.

text.p: Poland's inflation was higher than targeted last year but was not a cause for worry as long as it keeps falling and the economy grows fast, the World Bank representative in Poland said.
Paul Knotter told the Nowa Europa daily in an interview, however, that Poland would have to bring inflation down to Western European levels before it enters the European Union.
"It does not worry me, when real inflation differs from government targets by one or two points. It is important to keep it falling and to maintain fast economic growth," Knotter told the paper.

Year-on-year inflation in Poland fell to 18.5 percent in 1996 from 21.6 in 1995. It is seen at 13 percent in 1997 although many economists say this is too optimistic given Poland's planned budget deficit of 2.8 percent this year.
"Inflation will have to fall to Western European levels when Poland joins the European Union, especially since it also wants to enter the economic and monetary union," he said.
Knotter praised Poland's economic performance, but stressed the need to complete the slow-moving reform of the inefficient social security system which currently put a huge drain on the economy.
